newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's capital market down in May.
newsitem.headline: Romania's capital market down in May.

text.p: An independent index gauging market capitalisation on the Bucharest bourse and in the over-the-counter (OTC) trading system shows Romania's capital market fell by 3.2 percent in May from the previous month.
The market index dropped to 1,136 points in May, 3.2 percent down from the previous month, a statement from VANGUARD securities showed on Monday.
But the index was three times higher than at the start of the year, when it was 356 points, which reflects a rise in the average prices of bourse and OTC stocks, the statement said.
Other savings instruments, including bank deposits, unit trusts or hard currency, failed to produce such growths in five months, Vanguard said.

It said in the last week of May, the stock exchange rose by 1.9 percent from the previous week to 881.7 points. Over the same period, the RASDAQ, the Romanian OTC market, fell by 5.94 percent to 3,298.9 points.
Turnover in the last week of May was 30.13 billion lei on the stock exchange, down from 42.25 billion the previous week, and 42.10 billion lei on the RASDAQ, some 34 billion lei more.
Volumes were on the rise on both markets, mainly thanks to waves of selling offers, mostly from small stockholders who got shares under the mass privatisation programme.
Romania launched a mass selloff late in 1995, under which Romanians could get up to 60 percent in around 5,000 companies in exchange for coupons and vouchers.
Market capitalisation on the RASDAQ is 9.7 trillion lei. It is 2.4 trillion lei on the stock exchange.
The OTC market lists around 3,000 companies, but trades an average 500 stocks per session. The stock exchange has 38 listings, four of which trade on the first tier.
Steel mill Sidex has the largest capitalisation stake on the OTC market, or 12 percent, followed by cement maker Romcim, with 11 percent.
Chemical plant Oltchim and Azomures fertiliser maker, both stock exchange first-tier listings, take the bulk of capitalisation with 26 and respectively 21 percent. ($=7,110 lei)
